source_name: ECB Data Portal — PCP dataset (card payments & cash withdrawals, incl. fraud), SI country tables
why_relevant: Harmonised, machine-readable country-level card/ATM/POS series for Slovenia, comparable across the euro area; also documents the multi-acquiring double-counting caveat that matters when reading SI terminal counts.

source_name: Worldline — Indicative Card Scheme Fee Rates, Slovenia (PDF)
why_relevant: Country-specific acquirer disclosure of Visa/Mastercard scheme fees applied in Slovenia, with a domestic-transaction definition. Rare hard pricing evidence for the SI acquiring stack; a versioned PDF that can be diffed over time.

source_name: Mastercard Slovenija — Medfranšizne stopnje in provizije (interchange)
why_relevant: Scheme's own Slovenian-language interchange disclosure page; the entry point to SI-applicable interchange rate tables and qualification criteria mandated by the EU Interchange Fee Regulation.

source_name: Visa Europe — Fees and interchange (country rate tables)
why_relevant: Visa's European interchange hub linking per-country PDFs of intra-EEA/domestic interchange rates; the counterpart to the Mastercard SI disclosure and the second half of scheme-side pricing evidence.

source_name: Nexi Slovenija d.o.o. (formerly Nets CEE / Intesa Sanpaolo Card) — company records
why_relevant: Business-register aggregator record for the SI arm of the Nexi processing group (activity code 63.100, parent Nexi Croatia d.o.o. za kartično poslovanje). Gives legal identity, ownership chain, headcount and filed financials for the largest international processor present in SI.

source_name: Sparkasse Pay d.o.o. — Diners Club Slovenija issuer site
why_relevant: The legacy Diners Club brand in Slovenia is now issued by Sparkasse Pay d.o.o. (Ameriška ulica 2, Ljubljana) as Diners Club–Mastercard products. Tracks the fate of a legacy three-party scheme brand, its merchant-acceptance network and consumer-credit intermediation disclosures.

source_name: Banka Intesa Sanpaolo (SI) — Activa card system operator & product disclosures
why_relevant: The Activa brand and card system (created 1992 at Banka Koper) is operated by Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, which performs the clearing while Bank of Slovenia settles daily via TARGET2-Slovenija. The bank's product key-information sheets carry Activa Mastercard fees and terms — the surviving commercial trace of the legacy domestic scheme.

source_name: Wikipedija (sl) — Sistem Activa
why_relevant: Compact Slovenian-language history and structure of the Activa card system (founded 1992 at Banka Koper; clearing by Intesa Sanpaolo, settlement by Banka Slovenije via TARGET2-Slovenija; covers Mastercard/Visa/Activa/Maestro/Cirrus/Visa Electron). Useful for glossary and actor-map seeding, not as evidence.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Nacionalni svet za plačila, meeting materials
why_relevant: The National Payments Council brings together the central bank, banks, Bankart and merchant/consumer bodies; published session materials are one of the few places where SI card-acceptance costs, instant payments and scheme developments are discussed with slides and numbers.

source_name: Kansas City Fed — Credit and Debit Card Interchange Fees in Various Countries (annual update)
why_relevant: Annual cross-country compendium that includes Slovenia's interchange caps/regime; a stable, citable secondary benchmark when scheme PDFs are hard to pin down, and a good consistency check on IFR implementation.

source_name: Worldline Global — merchant acquiring / financial-institution processing pages and press releases
why_relevant: Worldline is an active acquirer/processor in Slovenia (e.g. Bank Transfer by Worldline available to SI merchants since Aug 2024) and its press releases are the main public signal of country-level product launches and bank outsourcing deals in the SI processing stack.

source_name: Delo / Finance — Slovenian business press coverage of interchange and card fees
why_relevant: National business press is where SI-specific interchange/MDR disputes, Bankart ownership changes and acquirer entries surface first, often quoting figures not otherwise published. The archived Delo piece on IFR caps and Slovenia is an example of usable local commentary.

source_name: Flik Pay — official scheme site (Bankart) incl. FAQ and merchant onboarding docs
source_subtype: scheme product page / technical onboarding documentation
why_relevant: Primary scheme documentation for Flik Pay (the P2eM / e-commerce leg of Flik). Merchant onboarding PDFs disclose acceptance mechanics, participating banks and merchant counts (>2,500 merchants as of the March 2024 document), which is the best available proxy for A2A merchant-acceptance penetration versus card acceptance.

source_name: Bankart Open Banking API Developer Portal (PSD2 HUB for all Slovenian banks)
why_relevant: Slovenia's de-facto national PSD2 aggregation hub: one connection reaches all Slovenian banks' AIS/PIS APIs, plus value-added APIs (ATM network data, transaction reports). Bank-by-bank sub-portals (e.g. /sparkasse) reveal which ASPSPs are live, API versions, and outage/performance pages — direct evidence of open-banking API availability and usage maturity. The advertised ATM-network API is also directly relevant to the ATM/POS topic.

source_name: Slovenian bank open-banking / PSD2 developer pages (NLB, Sparkasse, Addiko, DBS, Delavska hranilnica, Intesa Sanpaolo)
why_relevant: Each ASPSP must publish PSD2 interface specs, test/production endpoints and statutory API availability/performance statistics. Those mandated availability and 'number of API calls' disclosures are one of the few hard quantitative measures of actual open-banking usage in Slovenia. Also flags which banks route via Bankart's hub versus their own portal (Intesa uses the group ISBD portal).

source_name: ECB Data Portal — payment statistics dataset (PCT), Slovenia series
source_subtype: supranational statistical data warehouse with API
why_relevant: Harmonised, machine-readable time series for Slovenia: SEPA credit transfers including the SCT Inst breakdown (CTS_SEPAI), card payments, e-money, ATM withdrawals and terminal counts. The only source giving comparable instant-share series across euro-area peers, and the correct base for computing how fast instant A2A is eroding card/cash volumes.

source_name: European Central Bank — instant payments / SCT Inst indicator pages
source_subtype: central bank policy and indicator page
why_relevant: Publishes the euro-area SCT Inst indicator methodology and monthly aggregation from CSMs, plus TIPS reachability reporting. Needed to interpret and validate the Slovenian '82% of credit transfers are instant' style claims and to place BIPS/TIPS connectivity in context.

source_name: European Payments Council — SEPA payment statistics and SCT Inst adherence register
why_relevant: The EPC scheme registers list, per country, which PSPs adhere to SCT Inst — the cleanest way to enumerate every Slovenian instant-payments-reachable institution (including savings banks) and to date each bank's onboarding. EPC also publishes SEPA-wide volume statistics used as denominators.

source_name: UJP — Uprava RS za javna plačila, eRačun services and recipient register
why_relevant: UJP mandates and operates e-invoicing to the entire Slovenian public sector; e-invoices reach budget users via banks in the interbank e-invoice exchange (run through Bankart) or via contracted e-service providers. UJP publishes the register of e-invoice recipients daily and the list of contracted providers — a direct census of the e-invoicing rail and its intermediaries.

source_name: AJPES — eRačuni service
why_relevant: AJPES (business register agency) provides e-invoice services and registry linkage for Slovenian legal entities; complements UJP on the B2G/B2B e-invoicing rail and is a stable government-side pointer to accredited e-invoice intermediaries.

source_name: EPOS — Center za e-poslovanje Slovenije (e-business centre), e-invoicing research reports
why_relevant: Industry body producing survey-based research on actual e-invoice adoption in Slovenia (a downloadable report 'E-računi v Sloveniji – Poročilo raziskave' was observed). Survey data fills the gap left by the absence of published transaction counts on the interbank e-invoice exchange.

source_name: mBills (Abanka/Petrol-ecosystem mobile wallet) — official site
why_relevant: Non-bank e-money mobile wallet competing with Flik and cards: bill/položnica payment, e-račun subscription, QR payment at Petrol, mBills Mastercard. Its merchant-location count (stated >1,500 locations) and product pages track the non-card, non-Flik wallet rail. Operator has an incentive to publish user milestones.

source_name: Valú (Telekom Slovenije mobile wallet)
why_relevant: Telco-operated mobile wallet, the other significant non-bank wallet in Slovenia; passed 100,000 users at end-2021 per press coverage. Telekom Slovenije is a listed issuer, so wallet user/volume figures can also surface in its investor reporting — a rare quantified view of non-bank wallet adoption.

source_name: Apple — list of participating banks for Apple Pay in Europe (Slovenia section)
why_relevant: Authoritative, continuously updated census of which Slovenian issuers support Apple Pay and with which card products. Diffing this page over time dates each bank's rollout precisely — the single best structured evidence of Apple Pay penetration in SI (NLB and Nova KBM confirmed listed).

source_name: Slovenian bank mobile-payment product pages (NLB Google Pay / NLB Pay, Nova KBM, OTP banka, Intesa Sanpaolo Flik page)
why_relevant: Issuer-side confirmation and dating of wallet rollouts (NLB Apple Pay Feb 2024; Nova KBM Google Wallet from late 2023 and Apple Pay from July 2024; OTP on Nova KBM's IT platform) and of Flik enrolment per bank. These pages also state which card schemes and account types are eligible — needed to model the tokenised-card versus A2A split.

source_name: Monitor.si — payments and fintech technology reporting
why_relevant: Slovenia's main IT/technology magazine; covers Flik Pay launches, PSD2 third-party apps and European wallet initiatives with more technical depth than general media, frequently quoting Bankart and bank sources with figures.

source_name: Slovenian business/general media payments coverage (Delo, Forbes Slovenija, RTV SLO, Siol, Cekin, Svet24, Žurnal24)
why_relevant: In the absence of an official Flik statistics release, operator-sourced figures reach the public almost exclusively through Slovenian media interviews — user counts (~776k–800k+ active users), ~1.5–2m monthly transactions, ~EUR 126m peak monthly value, ~90% still P2P, and the Flik/Wero/EuroPA strategic choice. These are the only public volume datapoints for the cell and must be captured with provenance.
